title: Unbounded ordinary quasi-coherent descent on a Zariski total site
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(W_i\hookrightarrow T)_{i\in I}$ a set-indexed Zariski open cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $T_n=\coprod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_n)\in I^{n+1}}(W_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap W_{i_n})$, with the usual face maps dropping indices. Use only injective order maps, the small Zariski ringed sites $(T_{n,\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_{T_n})$, their exact structure-module pullbacks, and the ordinary ringed total module category $\mathscr M$ with augmentation $a$ and exact evaluations $e_n$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal L\subset D(\mathscr M)$ consist of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology on each component scheme [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cart}}$ be its full subcategory of objects for which every derived transition $Lf_\alpha^*e_mE\to e_nE$ is an isomorphism. Then the augmentation pullback induces a triangulated equivalence
$$a^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cart}}.$$
Its quasi-inverse is the restriction of the ambient derived augmentation pushforward $Ra_*$, and its adjunction unit and counit are isomorphisms on these subcategories. In particular this is an equivalence on actual total derived objects and their morphisms. No lower bound, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or vanishing of negative self extensions is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D7V, lemma-equivalence-unbounded-one, applied to the Zariski ringed total augmentation. The verification is the Zariski Cech instance of spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 0DHF, lemma-coh-descent-qcoh-unbounded-for-fppf-hypercovering: affine Zariski objects give cohomological bound zero; face-only ringed total model is the one already recorded by lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category. This records the ordinary Zariski version on complexes of structure-module systems.

proof.text: Every tuple component of a face map, or of an augmentation component $a_n:T_n\to T$, is an inclusion of open subschemes. Its module pullback is restriction and is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives]. Exactness can be checked separately on the disjoint open components, since kernels and local lifts for epimorphisms are checked on an open cover. Thus all face and augmentation component pullbacks are exact. By [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category], $e_na^*=a_n^*$ and the evaluations are exact and jointly conservative, so $a^*$ itself is exact.

source.place: Tag 0DHF, proof Ad (1), specialized to Zariski open components; cohomology.tex Tag 01E1, lemma-cohomology-of-open.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal O_T)$ and let $\mathcal A\subset\mathscr M$ be the cartesian systems with quasi-coherent components. On any scheme, kernels and cokernels of maps between quasi-coherent modules and extensions of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel, lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-closure, lem-pc-quasi-coherent-extension]. Apply these statements to $T$ and each $T_n$. Exact evaluation and exact face pullback show that the transitions on a kernel or cokernel of a map in $\mathcal A$ remain invertible. For an extension, compare the two short exact sequences along a face: a kernel element in the middle maps to zero in the quotient and then vanishes in the left term; a target middle section lifts locally in the quotient and its remaining difference lifts locally in the left term. Hence its middle transition is invertible. Zero belongs to both categories and they are strictly full, so both are weak Serre subcategories.

source.place: Tag 0DHF, weak Serre paragraph; schemes.tex Tags 01IC, 01ID, 01IE (affine-local closure properties).

proof.text: For a cartesian system $F$, write $t_r:F_{i_r}|_{W_{i_0\cdots i_n}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{i_0\cdots i_n}$ for its vertex transitions. Define $\phi_{ij}=t_1^{-1}t_0$ on $W_i\cap W_j$. Compatibility with the three edges of a triple gives $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$. This includes repeated indices: the triple $(i,i,i)$ gives $\phi_{ii}^2=\phi_{ii}$, hence $\phi_{ii}=1$. The module gluing theorem [lem-weil-pbc-module-object-open-descent] gives $H$ on $T$ with $H|_{W_i}\simeq F_i$. It is quasi-coherent when all $F_i$ are, by the affine-neighbourhood definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Conversely restriction of a quasi-coherent sheaf is quasi-coherent by the same definition.

source.place: Tags 00AL and 00AM, lemma-glue-sheaves and lemma-glue-sheaves-structures; face-only cocycle verification supplied here.

proof.text: For any tuple choose a vertex $r$ and compose $H|_{W_{i_0\cdots i_n}}\to F_{i_r}|_{W_{i_0\cdots i_n}}\xrightarrow{t_r}F_{i_0\cdots i_n}$. The overlap equation $\phi_{ij}e_i=e_j$ and $\phi_{ij}=t_j^{-1}t_i$ make this independent of the chosen vertex. For each injection its transition compatibility follows by choosing a vertex in the smaller tuple and using composition compatibility of the original system. Thus these maps give $a^*H\simeq F$. A map of cartesian systems is determined by its degree-zero components; their overlap equalities glue sectionwise to one module map $H\to H'$, and the vertex formulas give all higher components. This proves $a^*:\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal A$. The same construction works for all modules, without quasi-coherence. Its inverse on a cartesian $F$ has on an open $V$ exactly the compatible sections of all $F_n$ over $a_n^{-1}V$: such a family is determined by the degree-zero sections and the pair equations, by the vertex formulas. These are also the sections of the ambient right adjoint $a_*F$, by the module adjunction. Hence the inverse is $a_*$.

source.place: Tags 00AL and 00AM, explicit gluing and uniqueness; all-degree extension verified by vertex transitions.

proof.text: For $G\in\mathcal B$, apply [lem-sfb-zariski-cech-module-derived-unit] to the present scheme and its very same open cover and face total augmentation. It gives the canonical map $G[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*a^*G[0]$. The result applies to arbitrary modules, so in particular to every quasi-coherent $G$ here. This verifies the degree-zero derived-unit hypothesis of the unbounded criterion; the underived heart equivalence alone would not verify it.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, injective resolution construction; cohomology.tex Tags 01EP and 01EQ. Small-Zariski face-only module version isolated in the cited node.

proof.text:
The small ringed total and component module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. For each $n$, [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] gives an exact left adjoint $\ell_n$ to $e_n$, since all face pullbacks are exact by step 1. Thus $e_n$ preserves injectives: extend an adjoint map across $\ell_n$ of a monomorphism and transpose back. Evaluating an injective resolution of $F\in\mathscr M$ therefore gives an injective resolution of $F_n$. Sections at a total-site object $V\subset T_n$ are exactly sections of its evaluation at $V$. Consequently
$$H^p_{\mathrm{tot}}(V,F)=R^p\Gamma_{\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{T_n})}(V,F_n).$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] the latter is the abelian sheaf cohomology of $F_n$ over $V$, with identity comparison in degree zero. The same comparison applies downstairs on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0DHF proof Ad (4), and lemma-sanity-check-modules; exact evaluation adjoint gives its face-only proof. sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree.

proof.text: Use affine opens in the individual tuple components as total-site basis, and affine opens of $T$ downstairs. Every open admits such an affine covering. Every covering of a basis object refines to a covering by affine opens, by taking affine neighbourhoods inside each member of the covering. By [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor], componentwise coverings generate the total-site topology, so the same refinements are cofinal there. For $F\in\mathcal A$ its $F_n$ is quasi-coherent, and [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] gives $H^p(V,F_n)=0$ for $p>0$ and every such affine open. Step 6 identifies this with total-site module cohomology. Downstairs the same lemma and step 6 give the identical vanishing for $G\in\mathcal B$. Thus each of the two local bound properties holds with $d_V=0$ and with the cofinal family of affine-domain coverings. This does not assert that intersections of affine opens of $T$ are affine.

source.place: Tag 0DHF proof Ad (4)-(5), affine basis; coherent.tex Tag 01XB, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-unbounded-descent-criterion] to $a$, with the weak Serre categories $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal A$. Exactness is step 1, weak Serre closure step 2, the heart equivalence with inverse $a_*$ steps 3-4, the canonical module derived unit step 5, and both local bounds steps 6-7. This gives the inverse triangulated functors $a^*=La^*$ and the restriction of the ambient $Ra_*$ on $D_{\mathcal B}$ and $D_{\mathcal A}$, with their canonical unit and counit isomorphisms. Finally [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] identifies derived cartesianness with invertible cohomology transitions because the face pullbacks are exact. Exact evaluation gives $e_nH^q(E)=H^q(e_nE)$, so $D_{\mathcal A}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cart}}$; downstairs $D_{\mathcal B}=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ by [def-pc-derived-category]. The equivalence is therefore on the full subcategories of actual total derived objects and all their morphisms, as claimed.
